title: presentation / render-context contract
description: Homepage render context — the deck, the availability rows, the authored case studies, and the homepage nav links. Decorates the canonical JSON Resume doc (contract/jsonresume.schema.json) and never redefines its fields; build.mjs shallow-merges presentation over profile. Held to the same string-audit lens as the canonical copy. The homepage opens with ONE positioning statement: basics.headline is the statement, `deck` is its single supporting line, and basics.summary is résumé copy that the homepage deliberately does not repeat.

banner.description: Profile banner content tokens — the strings the generated header SVG renders (banner.mjs). Colors come from brand design tokens, not here.

tagline.description: banner subtitle — one line under the name

stack.description: small-caps tech list rendered under the tagline

deck.description: hero — the ONE line under the headline. Names the fields the selected work covers; it does not restate the headline's thesis.

origin.description: one sentence in the record margin tying the architecture / sculpture training to the systems work. Personal texture, not positioning — keep it to a single sentence.

seeking.description: Availability — rendered as ruled label/value rows (STATUS · FOCUS · LOCATION), not as a filled callout panel. CONTACT is the canonical basics.email, not a field here. No promotional paragraph: each value is one line.

label.description: the STATUS row's value — what roles are open

focus.description: the FOCUS row's value — the fields, dot-separated

places.description: the LOCATION row's value — cities and remote posture, dot-separated

caseStudies.description: The homepage's authored dossier entries — the unit of professional value, replacing the repository card as the thing the page argues with. Each is numbered in render order and answers the same four questions, so the set reads as one instrument: what was wrong, what was done, what shows it worked, and which parts were the author's. An editorial set of three to five; a repository is evidence inside an entry, never an entry on its own. Every string here is audited exactly like the résumé copy, so a figure must be in data/audit/grounding.json.

name.description: the system's name — an org, a product surface, or a program of work

kicker.description: one line under the name — what the system is

problem.description: what was wrong, stated as a condition rather than a task

intervention.description: what was changed, in the author's own terms

evidence.description: what shows it worked — and, where the record is incomplete, what is still open

role.description: which parts of the work were the author's

links.description: public artefacts backing the entry. Omitted where the work is not public — an entry without links is not a weaker entry.

Homepage nav links (and llms.txt). Email is NOT one of them — it is the availability block's CONTACT row, sourced from basics.email, so the address renders once. The résumé contact line uses basics.profiles + the canonical email, not these.

colophon.description: "Built with" — the upstream tools that produce and validate this site (design system, gates, authoring vault, dev container), surfaced as a homepage colophon and linked to their repos. Each must be a real build input or gate; private repos are omitted (no dead links).

role.description: one line — what it does in the build
